title: Operator-driven immutable deployments — reference patterns for private installs
author: Marisol Chen
content:
Overview

This page describes the operator-driven immutable deployment pattern we recommend for Redwood private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It focuses on a controller/operator that performs atomic, reproducible delivery of runtime components as immutable artifacts (signed images + declarative CRDs) and provides safe roll-forward/rollback semantics, multi-tenant isolation hooks, and a warm-standby fallback path for critical customer-facing control plane functions.

Goals and constraints
- Enable repeatable, auditable installs and upgrades with minimal manual steps for field engineers.
- Prefer immutable artifacts (container images, signed packages) to in-place binary changes.
- Provide safe rollback and fast failover when upgrades regress latency, resource usage, or correctness.
- Minimize blast radius: support tenant-scoped rollout and operator-level canary controls.
- Work within private deploy constraints: limited outbound connectivity, air-gapped zones, and strict KMS/HSM key usage.

When to use this pattern
- Customer wants predictable upgrade semantics and strict image signing verification.
- Deployment target is air-gapped or VPC-only with operator-based lifecycle management.
- Teams require deterministic rollback without relying on cloud provider snapshot primitives.

High-level architecture (text diagram)
- Customer cluster(s) (Kubernetes 1.25+)
  - Redwood Operator (namespaced or cluster-scoped)
  - Immutable runtime artifacts stored in internal registry (harbor/registry mirror)
  - Control-plane components deployed as VersionedRuntime CRs
  - Service mesh sidecars (optional) and network policy for tenant isolation
  - KV cache migration job and state snapshotter (for stateful components)

Architecture responsibilities
- Redwood Operator:
  - Validates CRs, verifies artifact signatures, orchestrates blue/green-like swaps by creating parallel ReplicaSets and switching traffic via ClusterIP / Service endpoints or Ingress rules.
  - Runs preflight checks and smoke tests from the operator pod (local test harness).
  - Publishes rollout events and metrics to the local telemetry sink (or pushes to customer-approved endpoint).
- VersionedRuntime CR:
  - Encodes desired artifact (image:tag), config hashes, KV snapshot references, and rollout policy.
- Snapshotter component:
  - Produces point-in-time KV and local FS snapshots used for rollback. Snapshots are signed and retained per retention policy.

Prerequisites (table)
| Item | Minimum / Recommended | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Kubernetes | 1.25 / 1.27 | RBAC enabled, PodSecurityPolicy or PSP alternatives configured |
| Container registry | mirror reachable by cluster | Signed images (cosign) required for operator verify |
| Operator RBAC | cluster-admin / delegated | See RBAC section below for least-privilege template |
| KMS | Customer-managed KMS recommended | HSM-compatible key usage for signing and snapshot encryption |

CRD: VersionedRuntime (summary)
- apiVersion: redwood.ai/v1alpha1
- kind: VersionedRuntime
- metadata: name: runtime-<tenant>-v2
- spec:
  - image: registry.internal/redwood/runtime:2.1.0
  - configHash: sha256:...
  - rolloutPolicy: {strategy: "operator-immutable", canaryPercent: 5, maxUnavailable: 1}
  - snapshotRef: s3://snapshots/tenant-x/2026-07-20
  - verification: {cosignSig: "sha256:...", kmsKeyId: "projects/.../keys/..."}

Operator lifecycle: responsibilities and failure modes
- Install: operator is installed via Helm chart (signed package). The install is immutable; operator upgrades happen by installing a new controller image and reconciling CRs.
- Reconcile loop: if a VersionedRuntime CR differs from the observed state, operator will:
  1) Verify signatures and config hashes.
  2) Stage new ReplicaSet/Deployment with isolated nodeSelector/taints for canary workloads.
  3) Run preflight smoke tests (container health, prefix cache warmup, basic inference call).
  4) Switch service endpoint to the new ReplicaSet when smoke tests pass.
  5) Trigger snapshot expiry and retention pruning.
- Failure modes:
  - Preflight fails: operator aborts rollout and emits detailed events.
  - Post-swap latency regression: operator optionally re-routes traffic back to previous ReplicaSet and marks the new image as quarantined.
  - Snapshot incompatibility: operator refuses to apply CR until snapshot being referenced matches expected version.

Step-by-step deployment and upgrade procedure (field guide)
1) Preflight & staging (offline preparation)
   - Ensure registry mirror has the image and cosign signature.
   - Push signed snapshot artifacts to customer's snapshot store.
   - Run local smoke harness: ./bin/preflight-check --image registry.internal/... --snapshot s3://...
2) Create VersionedRuntime CR with rolloutPolicy: canaryPercent=5, maxUnavailable=1.
   - kubectl apply -f versionedruntime-tenant-a-v2.yaml
3) Operator stages canary on dedicated nodes and runs smoke tests (automated). Monitor events: kubectl describe versionedruntime runtime-tenant-a-v2
4) If canary passes for configured observation window (default: 10m), operator increases traffic per policy, otherwise it triggers automatic rollback.
5) Full rollout: operator waits for all ReplicaSets to become Ready and then prunes older ReplicaSets according to retention.

Rollback and recovery
- Automatic rollback triggers:
  - Failed liveness/readiness within warm window, or
  - 99th percentile latency exceeds configured threshold (see Observability section), or
  - Functional regression detected by regression-suite lambda run.
- Manual rollback steps:
  1) kubectl annotate versionedruntime/runtime-tenant-a-v2 redwood.revert-requested=true
  2) Operator re-applies previous ReplicaSet + snapshotRef and re-routes traffic.
  3) Verify via smoke tests and customer acceptance tests.
- Snapshot-based rollback: operator will restore KV snapshots into a parallel namespace before traffic cutover when stateful components exist. This prevents destructive in-place restores.

Day-2 operations and maintenance
- Observability hooks: operator exposes Prometheus metrics and events: 
  - redwood_operator_rollouts_total{status}
  - redwood_operator_rollout_duration_seconds
  - redwood_operator_preflight_failures_total
- Alerting recommendations:
  - P1: preflight_failures_total > 0 for 15m after a rollout starts.
  - P1: 99th latency increase > 2x baseline for 5m after cutover.
  - P2: snapshot retention behind expected schedule by 30%.
- Capacity considerations:
  - Canary workloads should be scheduled on isolated nodes with smaller GPU count to detect memory/caching regressions earlier.

Security and compliance
- Image verification: cosign mandatory. Operator refuses to run unsigned artifacts.
- Snapshot encryption: AES-256 with customer-managed KMS; snapshotRef must include kmsKeyId.
- RBAC: provide a least-privilege manifest (example below) that grants operator permissions only to manage VersionedRuntime, Jobs for snapshotting, and Service endpoints.
- Audit trail: operator writes an immutable rollout event with signed attestations to the local audit log (optionally shipped to customer SIEM).

Example RBAC snippet (least-privilege psuedo-manifest)
- apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
  kind: ClusterRole
  metadata: name: redwood-operator-role
  rules:
    - apiGroups: ["redwood.ai"]
      resources: ["versionedruntimes", "versionedruntimes/status"]
      verbs: ["get", "list", "watch", "update", "patch", "create"]
    - apiGroups: [""]
      resources: ["services", "pods", "configmaps"]
      verbs: ["get", "list", "create", "update"]

Troubleshooting checklist (fast paths)
- Operator not reconciling: check operator pod logs, verify RBAC errors, ensure controller image is healthy.
- Canary fails on cold-start OOM: reduce canary replica memory or use smaller batch size; run a preflight with reduced concurrency.
- Snapshot restore fails: validate snapshot checksum and KMS permissions.

Operational SLOs and thresholds (recommended defaults)
- Rollout success rate >= 99.5% over 30d window.
- Mean time to rollback <= 10m for automatic rollbacks.
- Snapshot restore test success >= 99% monthly.

Appendix A — compatibility matrix
| Component | Minimal supported | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Operator | 1.2.0 | features: immutable-rollout, cosign-verify |
| Control plane components | 2.0.0 | must support snapshot migrate API v1 |

Appendix B — example VersionedRuntime YAML (simplified)
apiVersion: redwood.ai/v1alpha1
kind: VersionedRuntime
metadata:
  name: runtime-tenant-a-v2
spec:
  image: registry.internal/redwood/runtime:2.1.0
  configHash: "sha256:abc123..."
  rolloutPolicy:
    strategy: "operator-immutable"
    canaryPercent: 5
    maxUnavailable: 1
  snapshotRef: s3://snap-archive/tenant-a/2026-07-20
  verification:
    cosignSig: "sha256:..."
    kmsKeyId: "customer-kms-key-123"
